version.value: Sarasate arrangement attributed by the catalogue discography
version.note: Both candidate matrices name Sarasate; the exact performing edition and transferred master remain unestablished.

performers.note: Pianist unresolved. Commons and i78s credit Percy B. Kahn; DAHR assigns Kahn to C-8813 takes 1–2 and Walter Golde to takes 3–6, but the file’s master is not known.

date.note: Commons gives circa 1906; 9 April 1910 is not established for this file. Victor 74052 also covered a 1906 Gramophone master and a questionable 1915 remake issue.

place.note: Candidate sessions were in London, New York and Camden; none is assigned to this transfer without master identification.

matrixTakeSides.note: The catalogue number alone cannot distinguish Gramophone 727c [take 1] from Victor C-8813 take 2; DAHR also lists take 6 but calls that issue questionable. No matrix or take is invented for the streamed copy.

credits.note: i78s is the source repository, not an identified transfer engineer.

date.note: No transfer date is given; the 2022 Commons upload is not a session date.

processing.note: No equalisation, restoration or speed correction is documented. Analysis-only chroma transposition does not change playback audio.

digital.format: Original MP3 supplied through Wikimedia Commons; historic disc transfer

composition.value: Historical Chopin composition; Sarasate arrangement identified by DAHR.
composition.note: Composition and arrangement rights are separate from the recording-specific publication basis.

recording.value: US public domain: sound recording published before 1 January 1926.
recording.note: Rule 2. Commons explicitly applies PD-US-record-expired to this sound recording, not a composition-only tag. DAHR documents pre-1926 issued masters attached to Victor 74052. The exact session remains unresolved; neither a new 1912 publication date nor a specific take is asserted.

rights.creditLine: Frédéric Chopin, Nocturne Op. 9 No. 2, violin-and-piano transcription attributed to Sarasate; Mischa Elman, violin, pianist unresolved. Victor 74052; source i78s via Wikimedia Commons. Session and take disputed; Commons states US public-domain sound recording.
